name: Non-syndromic Postaxial Polydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Postaxial Polydactyly

criteria.description: Presence of an extra digit on the ulnar or fibular side of the hand or foot
No associated systemic or syndromic abnormalities (e.g., no craniofacial, cardiac, or neurological anomalies)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an extra postaxial digit without associated syndromic features; family history supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid in confirming diagnosis but is not required.

imaging: Radiographs showing well-formed extra digit with bone structure on ulnar or fibular side
Absence of skeletal abnormalities in adjacent digits
genetic: Mutations in GLI3 gene associated with some familial cases
other: Physical examination confirming isolated postaxial polydactyly without syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies such as craniofacial, cardiac, or neurological abnormalities
Additional syndromic features like developmental delay or organ malformations
Extra digit located on radial (thumb) or tibial (big toe) side rather than ulnar or fibular side
Different genetic mutations and inheritance patterns

redFlags: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies beyond extra digit
Family history suggestive of syndromic polydactyly or other genetic syndromes
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
